topic: What would happen if 1 US dollar were equal to 1 rupee?
angle: Why exchange rates aren't a scorecard; what a 1:1 rate would do to exports, imports, jobs, remittances, fuel prices and savings; how RBI manages the rupee; purchasing power parity vs market rate; examples of countries with strong/weak currencies and what that does and doesn't mean.

topic: Who is Rahul Gandhi? Education, career and the 'Pappu' label explained
angle: Factual biography (family, education with verified degrees and institutions, career, offices held, Bharat Jodo Yatra, Leader of Opposition from 2024). How the 'Pappu' nickname spread online, what fact-checkers (Alt News, BOOM, AFP etc.) found about edited or false clips and claims attributed to him, and what research/reporting says about organised social-media campaigns in Indian politics. Present what critics say too (gaffes, election results) and how public perception has changed. Don't name any party as the source of a campaign; say 'a political party's social media cell' or 'organised online campaigns' and stick to what sources document.

topic: What is per capita income? India's reality and the K-shaped economy
angle: Definition and how it's measured (GDP vs GNI per capita, nominal vs PPP); India's latest figures from MoSPI/World Bank/IMF and world rank; why a growing GDP and a low per capita income coexist; inequality data (World Inequality Lab, PLFS wages, consumption survey); what a K-shaped recovery/economy means with Indian examples (premium vs entry-level sales, wages); what the government and critics each say.

topic: What is a dictatorship and how did Hitler come to power?
angle: Definition and types of dictatorship vs democracy; the step-by-step history of how Hitler rose legally then dismantled democracy (1933 appointment, Reichstag fire decree, Enabling Act, banning parties and unions, Gleichschaltung, control of press and propaganda, 1934 merger of offices); warning signs political scientists describe (Levitsky & Ziblatt etc.) stated generally. Historical and general only; no comparisons to any current Indian leader or party.

topic: Is controlling the news media a sign of dictatorship?
angle: How authoritarian regimes have controlled media (censorship, ownership, licences, ads, intimidation); difference between regulation and control; what India's Constitution (Art. 19(1)(a), 19(2)) and Supreme Court say on press freedom; press freedom indices (RSF, Freedom House) with India's latest ranks and the government's stated objections to them; how readers can spot captured media. General and factual; name no party.

topic: Does a leader who gives no press conferences avoid accountability?
angle: Opinion piece (label it as opinion in the first lines). Argue that open press conferences are an important accountability tool: unscripted questions, follow-ups, a record. Use facts: how often leaders of democracies (US, UK, France, Japan etc.) hold them, past Indian PMs' practice, what reporting says about recent practice in India, stated factually without naming a party. Then fairly give the counter-arguments (Parliament, interviews, rallies, social media, RTI, elections as accountability) and answer them.
